This just in: Game distributor you've never heard of is shutting down.

I'm having a hard time caring about this.

According to their press kit, they were founded in March of 2013. In almost three years of business, they weren't able to establish any kind of meaningful presence in the gaming community. Not talking about profitability, just recognition. They offered a platform of supposedly high quality indie games, some wishy-washy business about DRM-free, and just generally 3 years of "Steam already does it."

I never like to read about anyone going out of business but there are some pretty important lessons to be learned from this. There's a razor thin line between niche and pretentious and whichever side of that line you end up on, you still have to market the hell out of your business if you want to gain the kind of momentum that leads to a decent income.

some wishy-washy business about DRM-free

What people need to take away from this is that most consumers don't give a hot shit about whether or not the games contain DRM as long as it's transparent and doesn't interfere with playing the game. Hanging an entire business model on the idea of "look ma, no DRM!" isn't enough to compete with Steam.

Steam is successful because:

  • Their client is feature rich, and extremely focused on gaming
  • They make it easy to buy games
  • They make it easy to buy games for other people
  • They sell games you want
  • They have ridiculous sales regularly
  • Once you're heavily invested in a platform, you're unlikely to leave for a similar platform unless it's substantially better

Newell realized all this stuff very early, and put all the company efforts in to meeting those ends. The result? Steam is now the #1 distributor of games on the planet. Now if only the other media outlets would learn from his example.

I think the DRM line might have been more help to them if it had been firm, but every time I see it mentioned it's like "mostly DRM free" or "primarily DRM free". But yes, I agree, most people don't care about DRM. Old-school DRM like SecuROM will get developers lynched but the DRM we see now is trivial. I feel like they'd have been better off not even bringing it up.
